newsitem.title: CHINA: D&P affirms Total Access rating.
newsitem.headline: D&P affirms Total Access rating.

text.p: Duff and Phelps Credit Rating Co said on Tuesday that it had affirmed the BBB-minus credit rating of Total Access Communication Public Co's (TAC) U.S. dollar-denominated senior unsecured obligations.

The affirmation follows the government of Thailand's decision last week to allow its currency to float against other currencies, which spurred a significant 20 percent devaluation of the Thai baht against the U.S. dollar.

The de-facto devaluation caused an immediate rise in the cost of principal and interest obligations related to TAC's dollar-denominated debt instruments, which make up an overwhelming majority of TAC's debt capital, and its ongoing capital expenditure.
The company recently refinanced the majority of its short-term debt portfolio with proceeds from the US$400 million notes and bonds, which do not mature until 2001 and 2006, respecitively.
On the date of the Thai baht float, only 18 percent of TAC's total debt obligations were due within one year, D&P said.
D&P said it believes TAC can endure a sustained devaluation of this magnitude while maintaining bondholder protection measures appropriate for its BBB-minus senior debt rating.
Singapore-listed TAC is the second-largest wireless operator in Thailand.
